How OpenCode Loads AGENTS.md Rules

Put repository-wide instructions in AGENTS.md at the project root. Use a nested file for guidance specific to that folder and ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md for user-wide rules. OpenCode 2 combines the files it discovers. Check the version and workspace directory first when a rule is missing.

  1. Place global and project rules
  2. Diagnose missing rules
  3. Check CLAUDE.md fallback
  4. Add instructions through configuration
  5. Edit rules during a session
  6. See the OpenCode 2.4.1 results

What do you need to check?

Check workspaceCheck fallbackPlace the file

Where to put an OpenCode AGENTS.md file

Keep the root file focused on shared rules, such as how to build the project and what to verify. Put package-specific commands in that package. Use the global configuration directory only for instructions that should reach projects across your machine. Find its actual path with opencode debug paths.

# Project instructions
- Use the package scripts for builds and checks.
- Run the affected package's tests after editing its code.
- Change source files and regenerate build output where needed.

OpenCode 2 starts with the global instructions and then reads files along the directory path upward from the workspace. The official guide places the boundary at home for workspaces within home, and at the project root for workspaces outside home. In our outside-home test, the global file appeared before the nested file and then the root file. A file above the repository root was absent.

When OpenCode seems to ignore AGENTS.md

  1. Check opencode --version and where OpenCode started. In a monorepo, open the package directly to load its instructions at the start of the request.
  2. Check the exact file name, the location your OpenCode service uses and the files on the path from the workspace upward. A descendant folder can contribute later when the agent explores that folder. Our root-start test did not load descendant rules on the initial request.
  3. Check whether the process started with OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1. OpenCode documents that it skips project discovery while retaining global instructions. For files configured explicitly, check which settings files were actually loaded.

Keep instructions compatible across scopes. OpenCode combines them and leaves any conflicting wording for the model to interpret. Use OpenCode permissions for actions that must require approval or be denied.

When OpenCode uses CLAUDE.md

In OpenCode 2, a folder with both names uses its AGENTS.md. A different folder that has only CLAUDE.md can still contribute its own rules. With no global AGENTS.md, OpenCode can read ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md.

To skip that fallback in OpenCode 2, set OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT=1 for the server and restart it. Our isolated test excluded both the global and project CLAUDE.md markers while retaining native OpenCode files. V1 used a different lookup rule. Check the migration guide if you still use V1.

Add extra rule files through opencode.jsonc

Use instructions to include an existing guide. Add the entry to your current config and keep other settings.

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "instructions": ["docs/team.md"]
}

Relative paths are resolved from the workspace upward toward the project root. OpenCode also documents glob patterns and absolute paths. In our test, docs/team.md appeared after the discovered files. Keep credentials and private data outside instruction files because the selected model provider can receive their content.

Check instruction updates in an existing session

OpenCode detects supported instruction file changes before the next prompt. In our test, editing the package file and continuing the same session in a new CLI invocation added the new marker to the next request. The old marker was still visible in the same request history. If earlier instructions would confuse a fresh test, start a new session from the target directory.

To make sure you are continuing the intended session, check the OpenCode session ID and its history.

packages/webGlobal → web → packages fallback → root → configured file
packages/web/deepGlobal → deep → web → packages fallback → root → configured file

We ran the macOS arm64 CLI in temporary workspaces with loopback-only networking. A synthetic provider captured only the published markers and returned fixed text. The test measures what OpenCode sent. Later tool-driven file discovery and model compliance were outside the test.
